title: Preparation of scFv stabilized chromatosomes for single-particle cryo-EM structure determination
protocol: Transform 1 μl pETHis6TEV-scFv plasmid into 20 μl BL21(DE3) RIPL cells following the manufacturer’s protocol.
Spread approximately 20 μL transformed cells onto an LB agar plate containing 100 μg/mL ampicillin.
Incubate the plate at 37°C for 18 hours.
Inoculate a single colony into 10 mL LB medium containing 100 μg/mL ampicillin and grow in a 37°C incubator shaker at 220 rpm for 14 hours.
Dilute the 10 mL LB cell culture into 1 L of 2x YT medium containing 100 μg/mL ampicillin.
Continue to grow until the OD600 of the cell culture reaches 0.8.
Cool the cell culture and the incubator shaker to 25°C.
Add 0.5 mM IPTG to induce protein expression.
Grow the cells in the 25°C incubator shaker at 220 rpm for 16 hours.
Harvest the cells by centrifugation at 3000xg, 10 minutes at 4°C.
Resuspend the harvested cells in 35 mL of Lysis buffer.
Add 0.5 mL of a 50 mg/mL lysozyme stock solution to the resuspended cells.
Freeze the cell suspension on dry ice.
Thaw the frozen cells in a 42°C water bath.
Use a Misonix sonicator for 4 minutes (15 seconds ON, 1 minute OFF with 15% power level) while keeping the sample on ice to break up the sticky cell lysate.
Pellet inclusion bodies by centrifugation at 27,000xg for 20 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in wash buffer (50 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.5, 100 mM NaCl, 1 mM EDTA, 1% Triton X-100).
If necessary, break up the sticky pellet with sonication for 30 seconds.
Collect inclusion body pellets by centrifugation.
Wash the pellet two more times using lysis buffer and collect the inclusion body pellets.
Add 4 mL of B-per bacterial protein extraction reagent containing 500 μg lysozyme and 20 U DNase I per gram of wet cells to the bacterial cell pellet.
Gently shake for 10 minutes.
Collect pellets by centrifugation at 14,500xg for 20 minutes.
Suspend pellets in 15 mL of B-per reagent diluted 10 fold.
Gently shake for 10 minutes.
Collect inclusion body pellets by centrifugation at 14,500xg for 20 minutes.
Dissolve the inclusion body pellet with 10 mL denaturation buffer containing 6 M guanidine hydrochloride and 2 mM EDTA.
Add DTE to a final concentration of 10 mg/mL.
Break up the pellet briefly using a ceramic rod.
Shake with a BenchWaver 3D Rocker at 66 rpm for 16 hours.
Clear the solution by centrifugation at 130,000xg, 10°C for 1 hour.
Add oxidized glutathione powder to the chilled scFv refolding buffer to achieve a final concentration of 551 mg/L.
Stir the buffer with a magnetic stirring bar at 600 rpm.
Quickly add 10 mL of supernatant from step 11 to 1 L of refolding buffer in a glass beaker and continue stirring for 2–3 minutes.
Cover the beaker with aluminum foil.
Incubate the refolding solution in a 10°C refrigerator without stirring for ∼48 hours.
Prepare 2 x 4.5 L dialysis buffer (20 mM Tris-HCl, pH7.4) and chill to 4°C.
Add 30.6 g urea powder to the dialysis buffer.
Dialyze 1 L of refolding solution against 4.5 L of dialysis buffer using 6-8 kDa cut-off dialysis tubing for 16 hours.
Replace with fresh dialysis buffer and add 30.6 g urea powder again.
Perform another round of dialysis for 16 hours.
Collect all of the refolding solution in a 2 L beaker, adjust pH to around 7.8 by adding approximately 2.6 mL of 35% HCl at 4°C.
Remove aggregates from the supernatant by centrifugation at 4000xg, 4°C for 10 minutes.
Filter the supernatant through a 0.22 μm filter unit.
Equilibrate 4 mL SP Sepharose Fast Flow resin with 20 mL of SP binding buffer (20 mM Tris–HCl, pH 7.4).
Stir the resin using a magnetic stir bar at 150 rpm and let scFv bind to the SP resin for 1 hour at 4°C.
Pass the solution through an Econo column.
Save the flow-through temporarily.
Wash the resin in the column with a total of 150 mL SP binding buffer (10 mL each, 15 times).
Wash the resin twice using binding buffer containing 100 mM NaCl.
Elute the scFv with 48 mL SP elution buffer (20 mM Tris–HCl, pH 7.4, 300 mM NaCl; 8 mL each, 6 times).
Check the OD280 of each elution fraction.
Analyze each fraction and the flow-through on an SDS PAGE gel.
Discard the flow-through if there is no more scFv in it.
Equilibrate a 5-mL Histrap column with 5 column volumes of Histrap wash buffer (20 mM Tris–HCl, pH 7.4, 40 mM Imidazole, 300 mM NaCl).
Combine all fractions from step 19 that contain scFv.
Add 1/10 v/v of Histrap elution buffer to the sample (final imidazole concentration should be around 44 mM).
Inject the sample into a 5 mL pre-equilibrated Histrap column.
Wash with 5 volumes of Histrap wash buffer.
Elute by linearly increasing the imidazole concentration from 40 mM to 250 mM over 20 column volumes using an AKTA FPLC.
Collect fractions from the main elution peak around 80 mL.
Check each fraction on an SDS PAGE gel.
Combine the fractions containing scFv.
Concentrate the combined fractions to approximately 4 mL.
Equilibrate the Superdex S75 10/600 column with Gel-Filtration buffer A for 2 column volumes.
Inject 2 mL of the scFv sample to the Superdex S75 10/600 column with a flow rate of 1 mL/min.
Concentrate peak fractions to approximately 1.5 mL volume using a 10 kDa cut-off Amicon concentration device.
Store concentrated scFv at 4°C refrigerator.
Dissolve approximately 5 mg H1 and ProTα protein powder in 0.5 mL nuclease-free water by rocking for 30 minutes.
Mix dissolved H1 and ProTα with 0.5 mL gel filtration buffer B (20 mM Tris-HCl, pH 7.4, 1 mM EDTA, and 600 mM NaCl).
Remove aggregates by centrifugation at 27,000xg, 4°C for 15 minutes.
Inject the supernatant onto a Superdex S75 10/300GL Increase column pre-equilibrated in gel filtration buffer B.
Run the injection at 0.75 mL/min using an AKTA FPLC.
Collect peak fractions and measure protein concentration.
Cast a 4.8% native PAGE gel.
Pre-run the gel in 0.2x TBE at 120V, 4°C for 2 hours.
Dilute nucleosome to 1 μM with TEN10 buffer.
Dilute ProTα to 2 μM with TEN10 buffer.
Dilute H1 to 1 μM with TEN10 buffer.
Titrate 100 nM nucleosome with 50, 75, 100, 125, 150, 175, or 200 nM of H1 in the presence of 200 nM ProTα and 2% Ficoll 400.
Adjust the final volume of each binding reaction to 10 μL.
Incubate the reactions at 25°C for 15 minutes.
Load 5 μL of each reaction on a 4.8% native PAGE gel.
Run the gel in 0.2x TBE buffer at 100 V for 120 minutes at 4°C.
Stain the gel with Midori Green Advance stain.
Visualize the gel using a ChemiDoc gel imaging system.
Determine the best ratio for the nucleosome and H1.
Use that ratio to make a large volume (>100 μL) of chromatosome by titration of the nucleosome with H1, in the presence of ProTα.
Dilute scFv with TEN10 buffer to a concentration of around 0.5 uM.
Add 3x molar ratio of scFv to the chromatosome sample and incubate on ice for 15 min.
Concentrate the complex to around 500 μL.
Inject the complex onto a Superose 6 10/300GL column pre-equilibrated with TEN10 buffer.
Run the column at 0.5 mL/min using an AKTA FPLC.
Collect the peak fraction and concentrate it to ∼100 μL using an Amicon Ultra 30K MWCO centrifugal filter unit.
Measure the concentration of the scFv-bound chromatosome.
Adjust the concentration to 4–5 uM with TEN10 buffer for sample vitrification.
Prepare liquid nitrogen cooled ethane and set the operation parameters of the Vitrobot Mark IV (Thermo Fisher Scientific) to 4°C, 100% humidity, 3 s blotting time.
Pretreat Quantifoil 1.2/1.3 holy carbon copper grids at 15 mA for 60 s using an easiGlow Glow Discharge Cleaning System.
Apply 3 μL of the chromatosome sample to the grid.
Blot and vitrify the grid using the Vitrobot.
Transfer and store the grid in a liquid nitrogen tank.
Assemble the grid with a clip ring and a C-shape spring in the “auto-grid” cartridge system for electron microscopes with an autoloading system.
Insert the grid into the electron microscope by the autoloader.
Screen the grids using SerialEM.
For traditional electron microscopes with side-entry, chill the workstation with liquid nitrogen.
Carefully transfer the grid to the tip of the cryo-holder and secure the grid with the clip ring.
With the grid covered by the shutter, promptly insert the holder into the microscope from the side-entry.
The grid is then ready for screening.
